title: SFX and Audio
author: coopykins
selftext:
Hey people, 

I've been doing games for a while. With the recent models you can get really good results both visually and technically, however I feel Audio is still behind. Particularly SFX, which makes a huge difference, in my opinion.

What do you guys do to fill this gap?

I was checking out Elevenlabs SFX generator but it feels really poor, maybe I haven't tried enough.

Otherwise I'm mostly looking into sound libraries, which is a quite tedious process.

comments.author: Don_InterestingSys
comments.body:
I had a lot of success asking the AI to look for open source sound clips (that I can use with attribution) it builds a sound board for me that I listen to and reject or keep with comments on the board.  I needed dog sounds and goose sounds for my game and ended up with a huge variety which let me range from sleeping to excited, playing, angry, etc.  I'm pretty pleased with the outcome.

I've also used Fish Audio to generate voices.  that's a bit of a learning curve but with some experimentation and about $5 I got solid results there too

replies.author: coopykins
replies.body: Yeah sometimes I ask it to find free sounds, but the results are so so, since it has not way to checking them. Free sounds at the end of the day have a verify large variance of quality, but for sure, at least you can find some stuff.

replies.author: Don_InterestingSys
replies.body: I find that when I do this I spend an hour or two listening to clips.  and yeah, sometimes the clips are all terrible.

comments.author: Entropydemic
comments.body:
There's free sound effects websites that require nothing more than to sign up. You can also imitate sound effects and record them yourself with your mobile.

Also, Gemini has this habit of never listening to me when I request no sound effects when asking it to make videos, often putting in isolated sound effects in that I should probably save and use later.

https://reddit.com/link/1y26tdh/video/8naeqpdq413i1/player

comments.author: FreeQ1337
comments.body: Have you tried to hook your AI into elevenlabs or gone by hand? Its pretty good when you can describe what you want closely. And its cheap tbh.

replies.author: coopykins
replies.body: Mostly trying by hand in the elevenlabs site. Maybe the kind I wanted to make was just too specific and they didnt have enough samples of that kind to make good results.

replies.author: FreeQ1337
replies.body: Go woth hooked up ai. Claude worked great for me. Max second or third iteration and i got what i wanted.

replies.author: coopykins
replies.body: Will try it, thanks for the tip!

comments.author: ipreuss
comments.body:
Elevenlabs always sounds to harsh for my taste. 

I got some sfx from free websites, but that was a lot of work and not always satisfying. I now got two huge sfx bundles from humble bundle, and that works great so far.

comments.author: jungle_jimjim
comments.body: I made a sci fi sfx sound generator with google ai studio. It generates sfx which you can then tweak. Gemini is really good at things like this

replies.author: dreamer_2142
replies.body: Would you mind sharing more about this?

comments.author: dr0idattack137
comments.body: I use the local SDXL model

comments.author: TheGAFF
comments.body:
I've had a lot of success with MOSS-SoundEffect v2. I made a Codex skill to use it and generate audio for the sound I want. The quality is good, but it can be kind of hard to get the sound you are looking for, so I tend to generate ~10 at a time for each sound I want and pick one from the list.

https://github.com/OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS/tree/main/moss_soundeffect_v2

replies.author: coopykins
replies.body: Interesting, Ill give it a look
